consensus_summary: Heaven primarily signifies the transcendent dwelling place of God (throne, presence, glory, rule) and, derivatively, the eternal destiny/home of the redeemed in unbroken fellowship; the term is also commonly the physical sky/firmament, a metonym for God’s reign (“kingdom of heaven”), an intermediate state, or the sphere joined to renewed earth.
book_summary: Heaven is the jurisdiction where God’s will is already done, covering both the visible sky and the seat of rule; Scripture’s saving movement proceeds downward from heaven to earth.
consensus_core_identification: transcendent dwelling-place/realm of God and eschatological home of the redeemed
book_core_identification: jurisdiction where God’s will is already done (visible sky + seat of rule), origin of downward saving movement
boundary_disagreement: Book elevates ‘will already done’ and the descent motif as definitional while treating sky and seat of rule as coequal; it does not center the redeemed’s eternal destiny or beatific communion that consensus treats as primary.
rationale: Both identify heaven as God’s realm (sky/throne/rule). The book preserves that general referent yet materially re-precision it as the jurisdiction of already-accomplished will and the source of downward salvation, thereby narrowing and reweighting the consensus core away from destiny/fellowship without replacing the category itself.
strongest_objection: Consensus primary sense as the redeemed’s eternal home and place of divine fellowship is omitted from the book’s core definition.
